thread.previously: Talks to end the Russia–Ukraine war are speeding up: Abu Dhabi talks, joint Ukraine–US–Europe talks on 16 November, and a Trump–Xi–Putin meeting in Shenzhen on 19 November. Meanwhile Russia hit two Kyiv bridges, and Ukraine hit the Kerch Bridge on 16–17 November. The damage is disputed. Russia has not agreed to Europeans joining talks.

stories.headline: Trump–Xi–Putin Shenzhen summit: no deal yet, and low expectations
stories.question: What did Trump, Xi and Putin actually agree in Shenzhen, and does it move Ukraine peace?
stories.dek: As of 18 November, nothing yet. The three-way meeting was set for 19 November. Xi and Putin met first. Officials played down a nuclear deal, and analysts expect little substance.

so_far.text: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022. The US is mediating talks to end the war, but as of 17 November the next round had no date. Trump and Putin last met in Alaska in August 2025, with no settlement. The fighting goes on. On 16 and 17 November Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge, which links Russia to occupied Crimea. Meanwhile China is hosting APEC, a yearly meeting of Asia-Pacific economies, in Shenzhen.

what_happened.text: On 18 November Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen for over two hours behind closed doors. Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov called the talks useful and friendly, covering global and regional issues. No joint statement was reported from that meeting. The first-ever three-way leaders' meeting of Trump, Xi and Putin was set for 19 November on the APEC sidelines. A US official said Trump and Putin would also meet one-on-one. As of 18 November none of this had happened, so no outcome exists yet. On nuclear arms, a senior US official said: 'We do not expect to get to any kind of agreement'.

steps.text: A peace deal needs Russia and Ukraine to accept the same terms, with outside powers backing them.
Shenzhen puts the US, China and Russia in one room, while Ukrainian and European officials meet in Berlin.
Russia wants China's support: analyst John Herbst says Putin wants Xi to back continued US pressure on Kyiv.
A US official calls Berlin, where Ukraine's post-war security guarantees are discussed, and China 'a coordinated diplomatic effort'.
So a Shenzhen outcome moves peace only if Kyiv accepts it and the fighting, which hit the Kerch Bridge on 16–17 November, stops.

history.text: This war began long before 2022. In February 2014 Russian troops occupied Crimea, and Russia annexed it. From April 2014 Russia backed militants in Donbas, in eastern Ukraine, starting a war there. In February 2015 Russia and Ukraine signed the Minsk II agreements. They were never fully carried out, an early lesson that a signature is not the same as peace. In May 2018 Putin opened the Kerch Bridge to Crimea. It became a symbol of the annexation and a military supply route. On 24 February 2022 Putin launched a full-scale invasion. Russia abandoned its push on Kyiv in early April 2022. In September 2022 it declared it had annexed four partly occupied provinces. On 8 October 2022 a truck bomb brought down two spans of the Kerch Bridge. It was attacked again in July 2023 and June 2025. In August 2025 Trump and Putin met in Alaska, but produced no Ukraine settlement. In February 2026 the last US–Russia nuclear arms treaty expired. The White House has now listed reducing nuclear weapons on the Shenzhen agenda. On 16 and 17 November 2026 Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge again, days before the leaders gathered in Shenzhen.

lesson.concept: How a summit becomes a real peace deal
lesson.big_idea: A meeting is only the first step. Talks must become written, signed terms, accepted by everyone who can break them, and then carried out. Most summits stop well before the end.

steps.title: A meeting is just talk
steps.text: Leaders meeting shows willingness, nothing more. Trump and Putin met in Alaska in August 2025, and it produced no Ukraine settlement.

steps.title: A joint statement is words
steps.text: A joint statement is a shared text released after talks. It is often general and not legally binding. The 18 November Xi–Putin meeting produced none.

steps.title: A signed deal sets terms
steps.text: A real agreement spells out specifics: lines, dates, who withdraws, who checks. The sides that are fighting must sign it. Russia and Ukraine signed Minsk II in February 2015.

steps.title: Then it must be carried out
steps.text: Signing is not enough. Both sides must act, and outside powers often give security guarantees, promises to protect against a new attack. Minsk II was never fully implemented.

steps.title: Everyone who can break it
steps.text: A deal holds only if everyone who can wreck it accepts it. That is why Berlin talks on Ukraine's guarantees run alongside Shenzhen.

example.setup: Imagine two farmers, Asha and Ravi, fighting over a boundary wall. The village elders meet to help. Let's see how far the dispute moves, one stage at a time.

lines.label: Stage 1: meeting
lines.calc: Elders meet over tea; nobody promises anything
lines.note: Shows willingness, settles nothing.

lines.label: Stage 2: statement
lines.note: Nice words, but the wall has not moved.

lines.label: Stage 3: signed terms
lines.calc: Wall moves 2 metres; Asha and Ravi both sign
lines.note: Specific, and signed by the two who are fighting.

lines.label: Stage 4: carried out
lines.calc: Wall actually rebuilt; elders promise to check it
lines.note: The promise to check is the guarantee.

lines.label: Missing signer test
lines.calc: If Ravi never signs, stage 3 fails
lines.note: A deal without one side does not hold.

example.result: Only stages 3 and 4 change anything on the ground. A meeting or a warm statement, even among powerful elders, leaves the wall exactly where it was.

apply.text: Use the stages on the news. As of 18 November, Shenzhen was at stage 1: Xi and Putin met, with no joint statement. A statement was expected only after the 19 November trilateral. Ukraine is not at that table; its security guarantees are discussed in Berlin. So even a Shenzhen statement would be stage 2, not peace.

practice.q: Suppose the 19 November trilateral ends with a statement that all three leaders 'support peace in Ukraine', with no dates or lines. Which stage is that?
practice.answer: First, it is a shared text after talks, so it is past stage 1. Second, it has no lines, dates or checks, so it is not stage 3. Third, Ukraine did not sign it. So it is stage 2: words, not a deal.

stories.headline: Iran targets US sites in Bahrain again; Indian sailor missing near Hormuz
stories.question: Why is Iran striking Bahrain again, and how exposed are Indian sailors and oil supplies?
stories.dek: Iran's Revolutionary Guards call their attacks on US sites in Bahrain payback for US strikes. Gulf waters stay dangerous: 24 Indians were aboard an attacked tanker, and Brent oil was $95.34 on 16 November.

so_far.text: The US and Israel began striking Iran on 28 February 2026, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. On 2 March Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz closed. A ceasefire and a June deal both failed to hold. In mid-November, CNN reported a possible Iranian plot against senior US officials, which Iran denies.

what_happened.text: On 17 November Iran fired drones at a US radar facility in Bahrain, its third attack on US military targets there since 14 November. Bahrain said it intercepted them. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a hit at Sheikh Isa Air Base; US Central Command called that false. The same day, US jets struck a Guards missile-launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island. Separately, the Tara Gas, a Panama-flagged LPG tanker, was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz off Oman, probably on 16 November. Of its 24 Indian crew, one is missing. Its attacker has not been named.

steps.text: Bahrain hosts US military sites, including radars, a helicopter base and Sheikh Isa Air Base, within reach of Iran's drones.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards call the drones retaliation for US strikes on Iranian communications towers and US drone surveillance.
The US says the drones were intercepted, and the same day struck a Guards missile site on Qeshm, calling it 'self-defense'.
Each round keeps Gulf waters risky for ships and crews; that risk may help keep Brent about a third above pre-war.

history.text:
The war began on 28 February 2026, when US and Israeli strikes killed Iran's Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. On 2 March Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz closed. That put world energy at risk: before the war, about a quarter of seaborne oil and a fifth of liquefied natural gas (LNG, gas cooled into a liquid for shipping) passed through it.

Pakistan announced a ceasefire on 8 April, but talks in Islamabad collapsed on 11–12 April over Hormuz and Iran's nuclear programme. On 13 April the US blockaded Iranian ports, so each side was now squeezing the other's shipping. In May, Trump announced 'Project Freedom' escorts for ships through Hormuz, then paused them two days later. The blockade stayed.

In June, Pakistan mediated a preliminary deal, announced on 14 June, and the Islamabad MoU, signed on 16–18 June. Yet in July the two sides traded attacks over Hormuz again, and oil jumped. In early October a third US aircraft carrier was announced, described as the biggest build-up since 2003. From 14 November, Iran turned its drones on US military sites in Bahrain, carrying the fight onto the soil of a country hosting US forces.

lesson.concept: How a sea chokepoint moves world oil prices
lesson.big_idea: Oil is priced on one world market. When a narrow sea route that carries much of it turns dangerous, buyers everywhere can end up paying more, even if most ships still get through.

steps.title: Oil has one world price
steps.text: Oil is traded worldwide, so buyers everywhere pay close to the same benchmark price. Brent crude is the main benchmark. It was $95.34 a barrel on 16 November, against about $72 in late February.

steps.title: A chokepoint is a narrow gate
steps.text: A chokepoint is a narrow sea passage that many ships must use. Before the war, about a quarter of the world's seaborne oil and a fifth of its LNG passed through Hormuz.

steps.title: Risk moves prices before shortages
steps.text: Traders buy oil in advance for weeks ahead. If a chokepoint might shut, they bid more straight away to lock in supply. So prices can climb on fear, before any barrel goes missing.

steps.title: Danger adds hidden costs
steps.text: Ships in a war zone pay extra insurance, called a war-risk premium. Crews face real harm, as the Tara Gas attack showed. Some owners avoid the route. Buyers end up paying these costs.

steps.title: Importers pay on every barrel
steps.text: A country that buys oil abroad pays the higher price on every barrel it imports. So its bill grows even when exactly the same amount of oil arrives.

example.setup: Imagine a small refinery that buys 1,000 barrels of oil. Before the war it paid $72 a barrel. On 16 November Brent was $95.34. Assume war-risk insurance adds $2 a barrel.

example.result: The refinery pays $25,340 more, roughly 35% extra, for exactly the same 1,000 barrels. No barrel went missing in this example; a higher price and risk costs alone raised the bill.

apply.text: This mechanism may help explain Brent at $95.34 on 16 November, against about $72 before the war. Iran declared Hormuz closed on 2 March, and attacks keep coming: drones at Bahrain on 14, 15 and 17 November, and a tanker with 24 Indian crew attacked off Oman. Each attack is a sign that the gate is still dangerous.

takeaways: A dangerous chokepoint can raise oil prices through risk, even when most ships and barrels still get through.
Iran's third drone attack on US sites in Bahrain and the Tara Gas attack keep Gulf waters risky.
Watch for the missing Indian sailor, any new Bahrain or Qeshm strikes, and Brent's next move from $95.34.

scenes.speak: इसलिए shortage से पहले ही, सिर्फ डर से prices बढ़ सकते हैं। Step four: खतरा खर्चा बढ़ाता है। जहाज़ों को extra insurance देना पड़ता है, जिसे war-risk premium कहते हैं। और crew को असली नुकसान का खतरा होता है, जैसा Tara Gas में दिखा। Step five: जो देश बाहर से oil खरीदता है, उसे हर barrel पर ज़्यादा देना पड़ता है।

stories.headline: Fed, ECB and RBI all lean towards higher interest rates
stories.question: Are the Fed, the ECB and the RBI all heading for rate hikes?
stories.dek: Broadly, yes. Fed minutes say December needs higher rates, an ECB policymaker calls a December hike likely, and Goldman Sachs expects 75 basis points of RBI hikes by mid-2027.

so_far.text: Inflation is back as the main worry. In September 2026 the US Federal Reserve (the Fed), America's central bank, raised interest rates for the first time in three years. Minutes of that 15–16 September meeting showed officials feared energy costs, AI investment and other shocks could spread into broader prices. In India, Goldman Sachs economist Santanu Sengupta said in October that he expected three more hikes by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) by June 2027. He flagged El Niño and rising crude oil as risks.

what_happened.text: On 18 November AP reported that Fed minutes say higher interest rates are needed in December, as inflation worries mount. Reuters said the dollar held near a 19-month high as US data supported the case for Fed hikes. Bloomberg reported that Boris Vujcic, Croatia's central bank governor, said an ECB hike is likely next month and more may follow. The Hindu reported that Goldman Sachs expects the RBI to raise rates by 75 basis points by April–June 2027. On 17 November Germany proposed Markus Brunnermeier for the ECB board, clearing the way for Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde.

history.text:
The European Central Bank (ECB) sets interest rates for the euro. It began in 1998 with Duisenberg as president. Trichet, Draghi and, since November 2019, Christine Lagarde followed. Each gets one eight-year term that cannot be renewed, chosen by the European Council. So picking the next president shapes policy for years.

The current rate cycle has roots in late 2021. In December 2021 the Fed projected three hikes for 2022. By January 2022 it signalled hikes starting in March. That ended a period of near-zero rates.

In 2025 India moved the other way. The RBI cut its repo rate four times, by 125 basis points in total. It went to 6.25% in February, 6% in April, 5.5% in June and 5.25% on 5 December. Cheaper loans were the direction then.

In September 2026 the direction turned. The Fed made its first hike in three years. Officials worried that energy costs, AI investment and other shocks could spread into wider inflation. In October 2026 Goldman Sachs's Santanu Sengupta forecast about 75 basis points of RBI hikes by June 2027. In November 2026 Germany named its ECB board nominee, easing the path for a new ECB president.

analogy.text: A rate hike is like pressing a car's brake on a downhill road. Press gently and the car slows without stopping. Press too hard and you stall the engine. That stall is the growth slowdown Goldman sees for India.

lesson.concept: How a rate hike cools prices and slows growth
lesson.big_idea: A central bank raises the rate it charges banks. Loans get dearer, people and firms spend less, and prices rise more slowly. The cost is slower growth.

steps.title: The policy rate prices money
steps.text: Every central bank sets a policy rate: what it charges banks to borrow money for a short time. For the RBI this is called the repo rate. In 2025 the RBI cut it to 5.25% by 5 December.

steps.title: Basis points measure the change
steps.text: Rate moves are counted in basis points. One basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point, so 100 basis points make one point. Goldman's expected 75 basis points of RBI hikes equal 0.75 of a point.

steps.title: Banks pass it on
steps.text: When the policy rate rises, banks pay more for money. They raise rates on home, car and business loans, fastest on floating-rate loans, whose rate moves with the market.

steps.title: Dearer loans cool spending
steps.text: Bigger EMIs, or monthly loan instalments, leave less to spend. Firms delay borrowing to expand. Demand cools, so prices rise more slowly. The cost is slower growth: Goldman sees India at 7.2% in 2027, from 7.9%.

steps.title: The Fed's move travels abroad
steps.text: Higher US rates pull money into dollars, so the dollar strengthens; it is near a 19-month high. Dollar-priced imports such as oil then cost more elsewhere, pushing other central banks towards hikes too.

example.setup: Imagine Priya has a ₹10 lakh home loan at an assumed 9% a year. Her bank passes on a 75 basis-point hike in full. To keep it simple, ignore her repayments.

lines.label: Hike in points
lines.note: 100 basis points make one point.

lines.label: New loan rate
lines.note: Assumes the bank passes on the full hike.

lines.label: Old yearly interest
lines.note: What she paid before the hike.

lines.label: New yearly interest
lines.note: What she pays after the hike.

lines.label: Extra cost
lines.note: About ₹625 a month less to spend elsewhere.

example.result: A 75 basis-point hike costs Priya about ₹7,500 more a year. Across millions of borrowers, that money is not spent elsewhere, which cools demand and prices, and slows growth.

apply.text: So when Goldman expects the RBI to raise rates by 75 basis points by mid-2027, borrowers like Priya would pay more and spend less. That is why Goldman also sees India's growth easing to 7.2% from 7.9%. The Fed, signalling a December hike, and the ECB, where Vujcic sees one likely, use the same lever.

practice.q: Same ₹10 lakh loan at an assumed 9%, but the bank passes on just one 25 basis-point hike. How much extra interest a year?
practice.answer: 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25 point. New rate: 9% + 0.25% = 9.25%. New interest: 9.25% of ₹10 lakh = ₹92,500. Old interest: ₹90,000. Extra: ₹2,500 a year, about ₹208 a month.

stories.headline: India weighs halving share-trading tax and raising derivatives levies
stories.question: Will India cut the tax on stock trading while raising it on derivatives?
stories.dek: The government is reviewing a plan to halve the tax on ordinary share trades and raise levies on derivatives. No decision has been taken, and one outlet disputes the derivatives part.

so_far.text: Securities transaction tax (STT) is a small tax on the value of every share or derivatives trade. Derivatives here means futures and options (F&O): bets on where prices will go. The government raised STT on F&O in 2024, and again in 2026 to curb speculative trading. On 17 November 2026 Reuters reported that SEBI, the market regulator, may also limit leveraged stock bets. Borrowing to buy shares, called margin trading, hit a record of about $15 billion in July 2026.

what_happened.text: On 18 November 2026 the Economic Times reported that the government is reviewing a proposal to cut STT on cash equity trades by 50% and raise levies on derivatives. No decision has been taken. Bloomberg reported the same day that India is weighing such tweaks. Zee Business, citing sources, said there is no proposal to raise taxes on derivatives. Officials are also considering a cut in long-term capital gains tax. On 16 November CBDT chairman Ravi Agrawal said STT and capital gains suggestions were under examination. Separately, on 18 November SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey ruled out immediate 24x7 trading.

steps.text: STT is charged on the value of each trade, so people who trade often pay it again and again.
Raising derivatives STT in 2024 and 2026 made speculative futures and options bets costlier to place.
Halving cash-equity STT would cut the delivery rate from 0.1% to about 0.05%, making ordinary share buying cheaper.
Together, the two moves would tilt costs away from short-term betting and toward ordinary share investing.
A cut in long-term capital gains tax would add to that pull, but nothing has been decided.

history.text:
The story begins in October 2004, when India introduced STT under the Finance (No. 2) Act 2004. At the same time, it abolished long-term capital gains tax on listed shares. A small tax on every trade replaced a tax on long-held profits.

In July 2024 the Budget raised STT on derivatives. STT on options premium rose from 0.0625% to 0.1%, and on futures from 0.0125% to 0.02%, from 1 October 2024. That Budget also set long-term gains tax on listed shares at 12.5% and short-term gains tax at 20%.

In September 2024 a SEBI study showed why traders' losses were a worry. Over 93% of individual F&O traders lost money in FY22 to FY24. Their combined losses were above ₹1.8 lakh crore.

The Budget of 1 February 2026 raised STT again from 1 April 2026, to curb speculative trading: futures to 0.05%, options premium to 0.15%. That made futures STT four times its level before October 2024.

By July 2026, borrowing to buy ordinary shares had hit a record. In November 2026, reports said the government was examining the other side: making ordinary share trades cheaper.

lesson.concept: How securities transaction tax is worked out
lesson.big_idea: STT is a small percentage of the value of every trade, not of your profit. You pay it whether you win or lose, so the more often you trade, the more it adds up.

steps.title: Charged on trade value
steps.text: When you buy or sell a security, the exchange records the value of the trade. STT is a small percentage of that value, collected automatically. Whether you made a profit or a loss does not matter.

steps.title: Each product has its rate
steps.text: Since 1 April 2026, delivery share trades pay 0.1%, futures pay 0.05%, and options pay 0.15% of the premium, which is the price paid for the option.

steps.title: Rates are a policy lever
steps.text: Raising a rate makes that kind of trade costlier. The government raised futures and options STT in 2024, and again in 2026 to curb speculative trading.

steps.title: Frequency multiplies the cost
steps.text: Because STT comes with every trade, someone who trades twenty times a month pays it twenty times. A tiny rate becomes a real cost for heavy traders.

steps.title: Profit is taxed separately
steps.text: Capital gains tax is a different tax, charged only on profit. On listed shares it is 12.5% for long-term gains and 20% for short-term gains.

practice.q: Ravi switches to options. He sells options with a premium of ₹20,000, ten times a month. What is his monthly STT at the rate since April 2026, and before April 2026?
practice.answer: Since April 2026 the rate is 0.15%: 0.15% of ₹20,000 = ₹30 per trade. ₹30 × 10 = ₹300 a month. Before April 2026 it was 0.1%: 0.1% of ₹20,000 = ₹20; ₹20 × 10 = ₹200. The 2026 Budget raised his bill by ₹100 a month.

stories.headline: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83, above range, despite AI selloff
stories.question: What does Anthropic's above-range $83 IPO price say about AI investor appetite?
stories.dek: Investors reportedly ordered six to seven times the shares on offer, so Anthropic could charge more even as AI stocks fell. Demand for this company looks strong. The first real test comes when trading starts on 19 November.

so_far.text: Anthropic, maker of the Claude AI assistant, filed its public S-1 offer document on 26 October 2026. It marketed 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT. In May 2026, private investors had valued it at $965 billion. Meanwhile AI stocks were falling. Forbes cites poor October earnings, worries about heavy spending, and Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation. OpenAI and other AI firms delayed their IPO plans.

what_happened.text: On 18 November 2026 Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its $70–$78 range, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC. Reuters and the Wall Street Journal reported the same price; the Journal credited strong demand. Orders reportedly ran up to six times the shares offered, one report says nearly seven. At 825 million shares, the base deal raises about $68.5 billion, or over $94 billion with a $26 billion private placement. The final share count is unconfirmed. Forbes puts the valuation near $1.5 trillion fully diluted. Trading begins on Nasdaq on 19 November.

steps.text: Anthropic's sales grew fast: third-quarter revenue was $17 billion, twelve times the level a year earlier.
Big customers multiplied too: those spending over $100,000 rose from about 1,500 to over 11,900.
The Wall Street Journal credited strong demand: orders reportedly reached six to seven times the shares on offer. Fast growth likely helped.
With orders far above supply, Anthropic could raise the price to $83 and still sell every share.
It did this during an AI selloff that made OpenAI and others delay IPOs, so the appetite looks company-specific.

history.text: Anthropic was founded in January 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees, including Dario and Daniela Amodei. In May 2021 it raised $124 million. In 2023 it released Claude and won big-tech backers. Amazon began investing in September 2023, promising up to $4 billion and making AWS, its cloud business, Anthropic's main cloud. Google put in $500 million that October. These deals gave a young company cash and cloud computing to compete. In March 2024 Claude 3 launched. In November 2024 Amazon invested another $4 billion, doubling its total. Then the price investors paid climbed fast: a $61.5 billion valuation in March 2025, $183 billion in September 2025 and $380 billion in February 2026. Not everything went smoothly. In February and March 2026 Anthropic refused Pentagon demands to drop its limits on mass surveillance and autonomous weapons. It was named a supply-chain risk on 5 March, and a judge issued an injunction on 26 March. Even so, in May 2026 it raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation. That last private price became the yardstick for the IPO. Anthropic filed confidentially for an IPO on 1 June 2026 and published its S-1 on 26 October 2026.

lesson.concept: How demand sets an IPO's final price
lesson.big_idea: In an IPO, a company sells shares to the public for the first time. It suggests a price range, collects orders, then sets the final price by how many investors want in.

steps.title: Start with a price range
steps.text: Before selling, the company and its bankers suggest a range: a band of prices they expect buyers to accept. Anthropic marketed its shares at $70 to $78 and planned to sell 825 million.

steps.title: Collect orders in a book
steps.text: Big funds and ordinary investors say how many shares they want. This list is the order book. Anthropic kept up to 20% of shares for retail buyers through brokers.

steps.title: Measure oversubscription
steps.text: Divide shares ordered by shares offered. If buyers want six times what is on sale, the deal is six times oversubscribed. Reports put Anthropic at up to six times, one near seven.

steps.title: Strong demand lifts the price
steps.text: When orders far exceed supply, the company can raise the price and still sell every share. Anthropic set $83, above its range.

steps.title: Price times shares gives value
steps.text: A company's valuation is its price per share multiplied by all its shares. 'Fully diluted' also counts shares promised through options. At $83, Forbes puts Anthropic near $1.5 trillion.

example.setup: Say a small company offers 100 new shares to the public, with a price range of ₹70 to ₹78. Counting the new ones, it has 1,000 shares in total.

lines.label: Orders received
lines.note: Far more than the 100 on offer.

lines.label: Oversubscription
lines.note: Six shares wanted for each one on sale.

lines.label: Price set
lines.note: Demand lets the company charge more and still sell out.

lines.label: Money raised
lines.note: At the top of the range: 100 × ₹78 = ₹7,800.

lines.label: Company value
lines.note: Every share is now priced at ₹83, not just the new ones.

example.result: Strong demand let the company charge ₹5 more per share. That brought in ₹500 more cash and lifted the whole company's value from ₹78,000 to ₹83,000.

apply.text: Anthropic's book was reportedly up to six or seven times oversubscribed, and it priced at $83, above the $78 top of its range. On 825 million planned shares, that raises about $68.5 billion. Like our example company, its value rose with the price: Forbes puts it near $1.5 trillion, above the $1.4 trillion target.

practice.q: Same company, but investors order only 300 shares and it prices at ₹78, the top of the range. How oversubscribed is it, how much cash does it raise, and what is it worth?
practice.answer: Oversubscription: 300 ÷ 100 = 3 times. Cash: 100 × ₹78 = ₹7,800. Value: 1,000 × ₹78 = ₹78,000. Weaker demand means ₹500 less cash and ₹5,000 less value than at ₹83.

takeaways: An IPO price follows demand: when orders far exceed shares, the price can go above the range.
Anthropic priced at $83 on 18 November despite an AI selloff, valuing it near $1.5 trillion.

stories.headline: Commander wanted over Kulgam attack killed; what India's PRAHAAR changes
stories.question: Who was Lateef Bhat, and what does India's first counter-terror policy PRAHAAR change?
stories.dek: Lateef Bhat, a 22-year-old Lashkar-e-Taiba commander wanted over the 11 November Kulgam attack, was killed on 18 November. PRAHAAR, unveiled in February, aims to stop attacks earlier, not just respond.

so_far.text: On 11 November 2026, a CRPF checkpoint in Kulgam was attacked and three personnel were injured. The CRPF is the Central Reserve Police Force, a central armed police force. Separately, two special police officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar, Babi Chand, 57, and Rashpal Kumar, 45, went missing on the way to an Army post. They were found shot dead on 12 November, and their service weapons were missing. Lt Governor Manoj Sinha and Chief Minister Omar Abdullah condemned the killings. Officials suspect militants, but no authority has named an attacker or group.

what_happened.text: On 18 November 2026, Lateef Bhat, a top Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander, was killed in an encounter in Kulgam, Mint reported. He was wanted over the 11 November checkpoint attack. Police say he was cornered in a mosque in the early hours. He refused to surrender, even after SSP Anayat Ali appealed to him on a video call, and opened fire around 2:45 am. Forces held back because it was a mosque. Two days earlier, he had escaped an encounter near the Laru bypass where another suspect, Umar Nisar Dar, was killed. Police also link him to a 22 July killing of a policeman in Anantnag and the 1 August killing of two migrant workers.

steps.text: Policing is a state subject, so local police are the first to respond to any attack.
Central forces like the CRPF back them up, and the NIA joins state police to investigate.
That system mostly reacts after an attack; PRAHAAR aims to act earlier, led by intelligence.
It targets what keeps armed groups going: money, arms links, online recruiting and over-ground worker networks.
Kulgam shows the reactive side at work: an attack, then days of tracking until the wanted commander was cornered.

history.text:
The dispute began in 1947, when India and Pakistan fought over the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. That war is the origin of the Kashmir dispute.

Armed insurgency came four decades later. In the 1987 state election, the Muslim United Front won about 31% of the vote but only four seats, and the result was disputed. In 1989 the insurgency began. In January 1990 the Farooq Abdullah government resigned, the Gawkadal killings took place on 21 January, and Kashmiri Pandits began leaving the Valley.

India's counter-terror system grew after big attacks. The 2008 Mumbai attacks led to the National Investigation Agency Act, which created the NIA, a central agency to investigate terror cases. A proposed National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) was never set up.

In 2016 the killing of commander Burhan Wani set off mass unrest in Kashmir. In February 2019 the Pulwama attack killed 40 CRPF personnel. That August, J&K's special status was revoked and counter-insurgency was stepped up. The Pahalgam attack on 22 April 2025 killed civilians and led to an India–Pakistan crisis. Operation Sindoor and a 'zero tolerance' line are cited as background to PRAHAAR, which the Home Ministry unveiled on 23 February 2026 as India's first national counter-terror policy.

analogy.text: The old model is like a fire brigade: it rushes in once a fire starts. PRAHAAR adds fire prevention: checking the wiring (money flows), clearing the fuel (recruiting networks) and fitting alarms (intelligence), so fewer fires start.
analogy.breaks: Fires don't plan. Armed groups change tactics when one route is blocked, and prevention can slide into profiling innocent people, as critics warn.

items.view: Calls PRAHAAR a progressive step, but says it is Home Ministry-led, gives no clear role to the armed forces or external intelligence, leaves political accountability unclear and lacks an NCTC.
Policing is a state subject, so central direction risks overlap and delay; state police lack funds and cyber skills; turf wars and profiling are risks.

These are proposals; no dated rule change has been reported.

lesson.concept: How India's counter-terror agencies share the work
lesson.big_idea: Policing belongs to the states, so local police act first. Central forces back them up and the NIA investigates. PRAHAAR tries to add a step before all this: stopping attacks early through intelligence.

steps.title: States own policing
steps.text: India's Constitution makes policing a 'state subject': each state runs its own police. So when an attack happens, local police are the first responders on the ground.

steps.title: Central forces back them up
steps.text: If local police need more strength, state counter-terror units and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) such as the CRPF join in. For the hardest operations, the NSG, an elite commando force, intervenes.

steps.title: The NIA builds the case
steps.text: Stopping the gunmen is not the end. The National Investigation Agency (NIA), created after the 2008 Mumbai attacks, works with state police to find who planned and helped the attack.

steps.title: A hub links the agencies
steps.text: Many agencies can mean confusion. The Multi Agency Centre (MAC), an intelligence-sharing hub, and a Home Ministry standard operating procedure (a fixed rulebook) aim to make them act as one.

steps.title: PRAHAAR moves the work earlier
steps.text: Steps one to four mostly react. PRAHAAR, unveiled on 23 February 2026, aims to be proactive and intelligence-led: cutting off money, arms links, online recruiting and over-ground worker networks before an attack. It has seven pillars.

example.setup: Imagine gunmen fire at a checkpoint in a made-up district called Riverpur, injure two guards, and escape. Follow the case stage by stage.

lines.label: Stage 1: first response
lines.calc: District police seal roads and hunt the gunmen
lines.note: Policing is a state subject, so they act first.

lines.label: Stage 2: backup
lines.calc: State counter-terror unit and CRPF join the search
lines.note: Central forces add numbers and firepower.

lines.label: Stage 3: the operation
lines.calc: Gunmen cornered; NSG called only if needed
lines.note: The NSG steps in for the hardest cases.

lines.label: Stage 4: the case
lines.calc: NIA and state police build the court case
lines.note: Proves who planned, armed and funded it.

lines.label: Stage 5: PRAHAAR's step
lines.calc: Trace the money, recruiters and online contacts
lines.note: Aim: stop the next attack before it starts.

example.result: One attack passes through many hands: local police first, central forces next, the NIA for the case. PRAHAAR adds the step that matters most: finding the network before it strikes again.

apply.text: In Kulgam, the 11 November attack was followed by days of tracking: Umar Nisar Dar was killed near the Laru bypass, and Bhat was cornered in a mosque on 18 November. That is stages one to three. PRAHAAR's test is stage five: tracing the money, arms links and recruiters who drew in a 22-year-old glazier.

practice.q: In Kishtwar, two SPOs were found shot dead and their service weapons were missing. No attacker or group has been named. Using the five stages, what still has to happen?
practice.answer: Step 1: no one has been named, so the first job is finding who did it; officials only suspect militants. Step 2: once suspects are found, they must be caught and a court case built (stages three and four). Step 3: PRAHAAR's stage five would then look wider, at money, recruiters and online contacts. Which agencies are now on the case is not yet reported.

scenes.say: Kulgam ke ek gaon ka 22 saal ka glazier, yaani sheesha lagane wala, ek wanted commander ban gaya. 18 November 2026 ko woh maara gaya. Kaun tha Lateef Bhat? Aur PRAHAAR, India ki pehli counter-terror policy, kya badalti hai?
scenes.speak: Kulgam के एक गाँव का 22 साल का glazier, यानी शीशा लगाने वाला, एक wanted commander बन गया। 18 November 2026 को वो मारा गया। कौन था Lateef Bhat? और PRAHAAR, India की पहली counter-terror policy, क्या बदलती है?

scenes.say: Hua kya? Lateef Bhat, Lashkar-e-Taiba ka ek top commander, Kulgam mein ek encounter mein maara gaya. Encounter matlab security forces ke saath goliyon ki ladai. Woh 11 November ko wahan ek CRPF checkpoint par hue attack ke liye wanted tha. Us attack mein 3 jawan ghayal hue the.
scenes.speak: हुआ क्या? Lateef Bhat, Lashkar-e-Taiba का एक top commander, Kulgam में एक encounter में मारा गया। Encounter मतलब security forces के साथ गोलियों की लड़ाई। वो 11 November को वहाँ एक CRPF checkpoint पर हुए attack के लिए wanted था। उस attack में 3 जवान घायल हुए थे।

scenes.say: Police ke mutabik, subah tadke woh ek masjid mein ghir gaya tha. District ke senior police officer, SSP Anayat Ali ne video call par usse surrender karne ko kaha. Usne mana kar diya aur subah kareeb 2 baj kar 45 minute par firing shuru kar di. Masjid thi, isliye forces ne khud ko roke rakha.
scenes.show: Refused to surrender; fired at 2:45 am
scenes.speak: Police के मुताबिक, सुबह तड़के वो एक मस्जिद में घिर गया था। District के senior police officer, SSP Anayat Ali ने video call पर उससे surrender करने को कहा। उसने मना कर दिया और सुबह करीब 2 बज कर 45 मिनट पर firing शुरू कर दी। मस्जिद थी, इसलिए forces ने खुद को रोके रखा।

scenes.say: Usse 2 din pehle, Laru bypass ke paas ek aur encounter se Bhat bach nikla tha. Wahan doosra suspect, Umar Nisar Dar, maara gaya. Police Bhat ko 22 July ke Anantnag attack se bhi jodti hai, jismein ek policeman ki jaan gayi. Aur 1 August ko Kulgam mein 2 migrant workers ki hatya se bhi.
scenes.show: Second suspect killed two days earlier
scenes.speak: उससे 2 दिन पहले, Laru bypass के पास एक और encounter से Bhat बच निकला था। वहाँ दूसरा suspect, Umar Nisar Dar, मारा गया। Police Bhat को 22 July के Anantnag attack से भी जोड़ती है, जिसमें एक policeman की जान गई। और 1 August को Kulgam में 2 migrant workers की हत्या से भी।

scenes.say: Yahan tak pahunche kaise? Shuru karte hain 1947 se, jab India aur Pakistan Jammu aur Kashmir ki princely state ko lekar lade. 1987 ke state election ke nateejon par jhagda hua. Muslim United Front ko kareeb 31 percent vote mile, lekin seats sirf 4.
scenes.speak: यहाँ तक पहुँचे कैसे? शुरू करते हैं 1947 से, जब India और Pakistan Jammu और Kashmir की princely state को लेकर लड़े। 1987 के state election के नतीजों पर झगड़ा हुआ। Muslim United Front को करीब 31 percent vote मिले, लेकिन seats सिर्फ 4।

scenes.say: 1989 mein armed insurgency shuru hui. January 1990 mein Farooq Abdullah sarkar ne istifa diya, Gawkadal killings hui, aur Kashmiri Pandit Valley chhodne lage. 2008 ke Mumbai attacks ke baad India ne terror ki jaanch ke liye NIA banayi. Ek National Counter Terrorism Centre ka plan tha, lekin woh kabhi bana hi nahi.
scenes.speak: 1989 में armed insurgency शुरू हुई। January 1990 में Farooq Abdullah सरकार ने इस्तीफ़ा दिया, Gawkadal killings हुईं, और Kashmiri Pandit Valley छोड़ने लगे। 2008 के Mumbai attacks के बाद India ने terror की जाँच के लिए NIA बनाई। एक National Counter Terrorism Centre का plan था, लेकिन वो कभी बना ही नहीं।

scenes.say: Phir cheezein tezi se badli. 2016 mein commander Burhan Wani ki maut ke baad bade paimane par unrest phaila. 2019 mein Pulwama attack mein 40 CRPF jawan maare gaye, aur state ka special status khatam kar diya gaya. April 2025 mein Pahalgam attack hua aur India Pakistan ke beech crisis aaya. Aur February 2026 mein aayi PRAHAAR.
scenes.speak: फिर चीज़ें तेज़ी से बदलीं। 2016 में commander Burhan Wani की मौत के बाद बड़े पैमाने पर unrest फैला। 2019 में Pulwama attack में 40 CRPF जवान मारे गए, और state का special status ख़त्म कर दिया गया। April 2025 में Pahalgam attack हुआ और India Pakistan के बीच crisis आया। और February 2026 में आई PRAHAAR।

scenes.say: Ab haal ki ghatnayein. Alag se, Kishtwar mein 2 special police officers, Babi Chand aur Rashpal Kumar, Army post jaate hue laapata ho gaye. 12 November ko dono ki laashein mili, goli maari gayi thi, aur unke service weapons gayab the. Officials ko militants par shak hai, lekin kisi attacker ya group ka naam saamne nahi aaya.
scenes.show: Kishtwar: two SPOs killed, weapons missing
scenes.speak: अब हाल की घटनाएँ। अलग से, Kishtwar में 2 special police officers, Babi Chand और Rashpal Kumar, Army post जाते हुए लापता हो गए। 12 November को दोनों की लाशें मिलीं, गोली मारी गई थी, और उनके service weapons ग़ायब थे। Officials को militants पर शक है, लेकिन किसी attacker या group का नाम सामने नहीं आया।

scenes.say: Toh India attacks ka jawab kaise deta hai? Policing state ka subject hai, isliye pehle local police action leti hai. CRPF jaisi central forces unka saath deti hain. Aur NIA state police ke saath milkar jaanch karti hai.
scenes.speak: तो India attacks का जवाब कैसे देता है? Policing state का subject है, इसलिए पहले local police action लेती है। CRPF जैसी central forces उनका साथ देती हैं। और NIA state police के साथ मिलकर जाँच करती है।

scenes.say: Lekin yeh system zyadatar kuch hone ke baad react karta hai. PRAHAAR ka maqsad hai pehle action lena, intelligence ke dum par. Yeh un cheezon ko target karti hai jo armed groups ko zinda rakhti hain: paisa, weapons ke links, online recruitment, aur over-ground workers jo unhe panaah aur jaankari dete hain.
scenes.speak: लेकिन यह system ज़्यादातर कुछ होने के बाद react करता है। PRAHAAR का मक़सद है पहले action लेना, intelligence के दम पर। यह उन चीज़ों को target करती है जो armed groups को ज़िंदा रखती हैं: पैसा, weapons के links, online recruitment, और over-ground workers जो उन्हें पनाह और जानकारी देते हैं।

scenes.say: Ab dekhiye, kaun kaun hai is kahani mein. Bhat ne college beech mein chhod diya tha, glazier ka kaam kiya, aur 2025 ki shuruaat mein ghar se gayab ho gaya. Reports ke mutabik uski recruitment The Resistance Front se judi hai, jise Lashkar-e-Taiba ka front kaha jaata hai. CRPF chief G P Singh ne forces ko badhai di. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha aur Chief Minister Omar Abdullah ne Kishtwar killings ki ninda ki.
scenes.speak: अब देखिए, कौन कौन है इस कहानी में। Bhat ने college बीच में छोड़ दिया था, glazier का काम किया, और 2025 की शुरुआत में घर से ग़ायब हो गया। Reports के मुताबिक उसकी recruitment The Resistance Front से जुड़ी है, जिसे Lashkar-e-Taiba का front कहा जाता है। CRPF chief G P Singh ने forces को बधाई दी। Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha और Chief Minister Omar Abdullah ने Kishtwar killings की निंदा की।

scenes.say: Scale samajhne ke liye kuch numbers. 2019 mein Pulwama attack ne 40 CRPF jawanon ki jaan li. Kulgam checkpoint attack mein 3 ghayal hue. Aur Bhat sirf 22 saal ka tha, ghar se gaye 2 saal bhi nahi hue the.
scenes.show: 40 killed at Pulwama; 3 injured at Kulgam
scenes.speak: Scale समझने के लिए कुछ numbers। 2019 में Pulwama attack ने 40 CRPF जवानों की जान ली। Kulgam checkpoint attack में 3 घायल हुए। और Bhat सिर्फ 22 साल का था, घर से गए 2 साल भी नहीं हुए थे।

scenes.say: Ab woh ek idea jisse sab samajh aata hai: India ki counter-terror agencies kaam kaise baantti hain. Policing states ke paas hai, isliye pehle local police aati hai. Central forces saath deti hain, aur NIA jaanch karti hai. PRAHAAR in sabse pehle ek step jodti hai.
scenes.speak: अब वो एक idea जिससे सब समझ आता है: India की counter-terror agencies काम कैसे बाँटती हैं। Policing states के पास है, इसलिए पहले local police आती है। Central forces साथ देती हैं, और NIA जाँच करती है। PRAHAAR इन सबसे पहले एक step जोड़ती है।

scenes.say: Step 1: policing states ki hai, isliye pehla response local police ka. Step 2: state ki counter-terror units aur CRPF jaisi central forces backup deti hain. Sabse mushkil cases mein NSG aati hai, jo ek elite commando force hai. Step 3: NIA state police ke saath milkar case banati hai.
scenes.show: Police, then CRPF and NSG, then NIA
scenes.speak: Step 1: policing states की है, इसलिए पहला response local police का। Step 2: state की counter-terror units और CRPF जैसी central forces backup देती हैं। सबसे मुश्किल cases में NSG आती है, जो एक elite commando force है। Step 3: NIA state police के साथ मिलकर case बनाती है।

scenes.say: Step 4: ek intelligence-sharing hub, Multi Agency Centre, aur Home Ministry ki ek rulebook koshish karti hain ki saari agencies ek saath kaam karein. Step 5: PRAHAAR kaam ko pehle le aati hai. 23 February ko launch hui is policy ke 7 pillars hain, Prevention se lekar Recovery aur resilience tak.
scenes.speak: Step 4: एक intelligence-sharing hub, Multi Agency Centre, और Home Ministry की एक rulebook कोशिश करती हैं कि सारी agencies एक साथ काम करें। Step 5: PRAHAAR काम को पहले ले आती है। 23 February को launch हुई इस policy के 7 pillars हैं, Prevention से लेकर Recovery और resilience तक।

Stage 1: district police raste seal karti hai aur unhe dhoondhti hai. Stage 2: state ki counter-terror unit aur CRPF search mein shaamil hote hain.
scenes.speak: चलिए try करते हैं। मान लीजिए एक made-up district है, Riverpur। वहाँ कुछ gunmen एक checkpoint पर firing करते हैं, 2 guards को घायल करते हैं और भाग जाते हैं। Stage 1: district police रास्ते seal करती है और उन्हें ढूँढती है। Stage 2: state की counter-terror unit और CRPF search में शामिल होते हैं।

scenes.say: Analysts ko kamiyaan dikhti hain. scenes.say: Ek aam galatfehmi: PRAHAAR Kulgam ka jawab nahi tha. Yeh 23 February ko launch hui thi. Aap mein se zyadatar par Kulgam encounter ka seedha asar nahi hai. Lekin PRAHAAR ke proposals aapke phone aur wallet tak pahunch sakte hain: extremist content ke liye platforms ki jawabdehi, decentralised finance platforms par sakht identity checks, aur crypto paise ki tracking.
scenes.speak: एक आम ग़लतफ़हमी: PRAHAAR Kulgam का जवाब नहीं था। यह 23 February को launch हुई थी। आप में से ज़्यादातर पर Kulgam encounter का सीधा असर नहीं है। लेकिन PRAHAAR के proposals आपके phone और wallet तक पहुँच सकते हैं: extremist content के लिए platforms की जवाबदेही, decentralised finance platforms पर सख़्त identity checks, और crypto पैसे की tracking।

scenes.say: Ab yeh lesson apply kijiye. Kulgam mein attack, Laru bypass ke paas chase, aur masjid wala encounter, yeh stage 1 se 3 hain. PRAHAAR ka asli test stage 5 hai: ek 22 saal ke glazier ke peeche ka paisa, weapons links aur recruiters trace karna.
scenes.speak: अब यह lesson apply कीजिए। Kulgam में attack, Laru bypass के पास chase, और मस्जिद वाला encounter, यह stage 1 से 3 हैं। PRAHAAR का असली test stage 5 है: एक 22 साल के glazier के पीछे का पैसा, weapons links और recruiters trace करना।

scenes.say: Nazar kis par rakhein? Kya police batayegi ki Kishtwar ke officers ko kisne maara, aur kya unke weapons milenge? Kya PRAHAAR ke proposals, jaise IT Rules mein badlav, sach mein rules banenge? Koi date tay nahi hai. Yeh bhi pata nahi ki 11 November ko Bhat ne khud firing ki thi ya nahi.
scenes.speak: नज़र किस पर रखें? क्या police बताएगी कि Kishtwar के officers को किसने मारा, और क्या उनके weapons मिलेंगे? क्या PRAHAAR के proposals, जैसे IT Rules में बदलाव, सच में rules बनेंगे? कोई date तय नहीं है। यह भी पता नहीं कि 11 November को Bhat ने खुद firing की थी या नहीं।

scenes.say: Teen baatein yaad rakhiye. Local police pehle action leti hai, central forces saath deti hain, NIA jaanch karti hai, aur PRAHAAR pehle hi action lena chahti hai. Kulgam attack ke liye wanted Lateef Bhat 18 November ko maara gaya. Aur nazar rakhiye ki Kishtwar ke hatyaron ke naam saamne aate hain ya nahi, aur PRAHAAR ke proposals rules bante hain ya nahi.
scenes.speak: तीन बातें याद रखिए। Local police पहले action लेती है, central forces साथ देती हैं, NIA जाँच करती है, और PRAHAAR पहले ही action लेना चाहती है। Kulgam attack के लिए wanted Lateef Bhat 18 November को मारा गया। और नज़र रखिए कि Kishtwar के हत्यारों के नाम सामने आते हैं या नहीं, और PRAHAAR के proposals rules बनते हैं या नहीं।

stories.headline: India–US deal called ‘99% done’ while UK-pact Scotch sits at ports
stories.question: Is the India–US trade deal really almost done, and why is Scotch stuck at Indian ports?
stories.dek: Not yet. An official called the US deal ‘99% done’ on 18 November, but it is still unsigned. Scotch shows why signing is not the end: customs must also agree on what a product is.

so_far.text: The India–UK trade pact came into force on 15 July 2026. It cut India's duty on Scotch whisky from 150% to 75%. Customs investigators then questioned whether whisky shipped in bulk qualifies. As of 16 November, no resolution had been reported. Meanwhile, the India–US interim deal, set out in a framework on 7 February 2026, stayed unsigned. On 15 November, Goyal said the US had agreed to give Indian goods preferential access.

what_happened.text: On 18 November 2026, Ashraf of ITPO told Bloomberg that the India–US trade deal is 'almost 99% done'. He gave no signing date. The same day, Reuters reported that India will charge bulk Scotch imports an effective 162.5% in duty and tax. That is above the 150% rate before the UK pact, and far above the pact's 75%. More than 80 containers belonging to Pernod Ricard, Diageo and Bacardi are stuck at Indian ports. The cause is a dispute over how customs classifies bulk Scotch.

steps.text: A trade pact lowers duty only on products that fit the customs category the pact names.
Customs investigators argue the UK pact's 75% rate covers only finished, bottled whisky.
Bulk Scotch arrives unbottled, for blending or bottling in India, so investigators would class it as a compound alcoholic preparation.
Outside the pact category, bulk Scotch reportedly faces 162.5%, so shipments wait while importers contest it.
The US deal is one step further back: India can cut tariffs only once it becomes a legal agreement.

history.text:
The story begins on 13 February 2025, when the leaders of India and the US launched trade negotiations. Formal talks began in March 2025, aiming to finish a first part of the deal by autumn 2025. That did not happen. Instead, tariffs (taxes on imports) rose. On 31 July 2025 Trump announced 25% tariffs on Indian goods from 7 August and threatened more over India's purchases of Russian oil. A further 25% penalty took the total to 50% from 27 August 2025.

On 7 February 2026 the two sides released a framework for an interim deal. The US cut its tariff on Indian goods to 18% and removed the Russian-oil penalty. India agreed to cut or remove tariffs on US industrial goods and many farm products, while protecting dairy and cereals. Signing was expected by mid-March 2026. But Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said India could cut its own tariffs only once the framework became a legal agreement. In November it was still unsigned.

A separate deal explains the Scotch story. India and the UK signed a trade pact, called CETA, in 2025. It came into force on 15 July 2026. It cut the Scotch whisky duty from 150% to 75%, falling to 40% by year 10. The bulk Scotch dispute arose under this pact.

analogy.text: Think of a coupon for '50% off bottled juice'. You bring the same juice in a big drum, to bottle at home. The cashier says a drum is not a bottle, so no discount. The coupon's wording, as the cashier reads it, sets your price.

lesson.concept: How customs classification decides the duty you pay
lesson.big_idea: A trade deal lowers duty only on goods in the exact categories it names. Customs officers decide which category a shipment falls into, so their reading can push the price up or down.

steps.title: Every product gets a code
steps.text: Customs sorts every imported product into a category using HSN codes, an international numbering list. Each code has its own duty rate: a tax charged as a percentage of the goods' value.

steps.title: Trade deals cut rates by code
steps.text: A trade pact lists categories and gives the partner's goods a lower rate. The India–UK pact, in force since 15 July 2026, cut Scotch whisky from 150% to 75%, falling to 40% by year 10.

steps.title: Goods must also qualify
steps.text: Goods must meet rules of origin, meaning proof they truly come from the partner country. One source says UK goods need at least 35% of their value added in the UK.

steps.title: Customs decides at the port
steps.text: At the port, customs decides which code fits. Investigators say bulk Scotch is not bottled whisky but a 'compound alcoholic preparation', outside the pact rate. Importers say it is still Scotch.

steps.title: The deal must be legal first
steps.text: None of this starts until a deal is a legal agreement. India's Commerce Secretary said India could cut tariffs only once the US framework became one.

apply.text: The UK pact has been in force since 15 July 2026, yet bulk Scotch is reportedly charged 162.5% because customs reads it as a different product. The US deal is a step further back: ITPO's Ashraf calls it 'almost 99% done', but India cannot cut tariffs until it becomes a legal agreement.

practice.q: The same company imports bulk Scotch worth ₹2 crore. How much more does it pay at 162.5% than at the 75% pact rate?
practice.answer: At 75%: 75% of ₹2 crore = ₹1.5 crore. At 162.5%: 162.5% of ₹2 crore = ₹3.25 crore. Difference: ₹3.25 crore − ₹1.5 crore = ₹1.75 crore more.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan now due between Narsapur and Puri on 20 November
stories.question: Where and when will Cyclone Akvan hit, and who needs to prepare?
stories.dek: IMD expects Akvan to cross between Narsapur and Puri around noon on 20 November. Winds are forecast weaker, but red alerts stand and isolated extremely heavy rain is forecast in coastal Andhra.

so_far.text: Akvan is the third cyclone of the season, after Arnab and Murasu. On 17 November, forecasts had it hitting the Andhra coast on 20 November, with Odisha bracing for heavy rain. At that point IMD expected a 'very severe' storm, with winds of 120–130 kmph gusting to 145. Odisha drew up a list of about 2.04 lakh people for possible evacuation. Reports on the morning of 18 November still placed landfall between Nellore and Visakhapatnam.

what_happened.text: At 9:30 pm on 18 November, IMD placed Akvan in the south Bay of Bengal, about 500 km southeast of Narsapur, moving north-northwest. IMD now expects it to cross the coast between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha around noon on 20 November. It is forecast to land as a severe cyclonic storm, with winds of 90–100 kmph gusting to 110, not as a very severe one. Red alerts cover north Andhra, Yanam and south Odisha. Odisha says over 47,000 people have been moved. Ganjam has moved 149 pregnant women to health facilities.

steps.text: Akvan is moving north-northwest, and IMD has moved the expected crossing zone north, to between Narsapur and Puri.
That zone covers north Andhra, Yanam and south Odisha, so the red alerts now sit there.
Landfall winds are now forecast at 90–100 kmph instead of 120–130, so the risk of wind damage eases somewhat.
But a cyclone's rain does not depend on its wind category. Extremely heavy rain is still forecast at isolated places in coastal Andhra.
Heavy rain inland causes floods and landslides, so Rayagada has mapped 55 landslide-prone and 148 flood-prone spots.

history.text:
Most of India's cyclones form in the Bay of Bengal: roughly four for every one from the Arabian Sea. Andhra Pradesh has faced severe cyclones before, including in November 1977 and May 1990.

The way Odisha handles cyclones has its roots in 1999. On 29 October 1999 the Odisha Super Cyclone killed roughly 10,000 people. The disaster pushed Odisha to create its own disaster management bodies. 29 October is now National Disaster Mitigation Day.

The difference showed on 12 October 2013. Cyclone Phailin made landfall near Gopalpur in Ganjam, and about 45 people died. Early warnings and mass evacuation are credited with limiting the deaths. Exactly a year later, on 12 October 2014, Cyclone Hudhud struck Visakhapatnam. Sources disagree on how many died.

You can see that history in how Akvan is being handled: warn early and move people before landfall. Ganjam and Visakhapatnam, both hit before, are again among the places being watched. Akvan is the third cyclone of the 2026 season, after Arnab and Murasu. On 17 November it was expected to hit Andhra on 20 November. By the night of 18 November, IMD had moved the expected crossing north and lowered the storm's expected strength.

analogy.text: Think of watering a garden. A strong jet from a hose hits hard, but you move on in a minute. A gentle sprinkler left on all night floods the bed. Wind category is the jet's force. Total rain depends on how long the water keeps falling.
analogy.breaks: A real cyclone brings wind and rain together, plus sea surge at the coast. Hills and sea moisture also change rain totals.

lesson.concept: Why a weaker cyclone can still bring dangerous rain
lesson.big_idea: A cyclone's category is set by its wind speed. Its rain is a separate threat: total rain depends on how hard it pours and how long the storm stays over a place.

steps.title: Category means wind speed
steps.text: Forecasters label a cyclone by its steady wind speed near the centre. IMD now expects Akvan to land as a 'severe' storm at 90–100 kmph, not a 'very severe' one at 120–130 kmph.

steps.title: Wind hits the coast hardest
steps.text: Strong wind tears off roofs, snaps trees and power lines, and pushes sea water onto land. This damage is worst where the centre crosses the coast, and it fades quickly inland.

steps.title: Rain is a separate measure
steps.text: A cyclone draws moisture up from the warm sea and drops it as rain from bands of cloud. These bands spread far from the centre, so rain falls well beyond the landfall point.

steps.title: Total rain = rate × hours
steps.text: The rain a town gets is the centimetres that fall each hour multiplied by the hours the clouds stay overhead. A slower storm stays longer, so it can drop more rain even with weaker wind.

steps.title: Rain floods rivers and hills
steps.text: Heavy rain fills rivers and loosens hill slopes, causing floods and landslides far from the coast. That is why alerts cover rain as well as wind.

example.setup: Imagine two storms pass over the same coastal town. Storm A has stronger wind but moves fast. Storm B has weaker wind but moves slowly. Assume the rain rates below.

lines.label: Storm A rain
lines.note: Fast storm: its clouds stay overhead for only six hours.

lines.label: Storm B rain
lines.note: Lighter rain each hour, but it lasts much longer.

lines.label: Compare the rain
lines.note: The weaker storm drops almost twice the rain.

lines.label: Compare the wind
lines.calc: Storm A higher, Storm B lower
lines.note: Storm A still does more wind damage, mostly near the coast.

example.result: A lower wind category means less wind damage, not less rain. A weaker, slower storm can flood a town worse than a stronger, faster one.

apply.text: So when IMD lowered Akvan's forecast to a severe storm at 90–100 kmph, the wind risk eased, but the rain did not go away. Red alerts still cover north Andhra, Yanam and south Odisha. Extremely heavy rain is forecast at isolated places in coastal Andhra on 19 and 20 November. Rayagada has mapped 55 landslide-prone and 148 flood-prone spots.

practice.q: Storm C pours 1 cm per hour for 24 hours. Storm D pours 3 cm per hour for 5 hours. Which drops more rain on a town?
practice.answer: Storm C: 1 cm × 24 hours = 24 cm. Storm D: 3 cm × 5 hours = 15 cm. Storm C drops 9 cm more. Its rain is lighter each hour, but it lasts almost five times as long.

scenes.say: Akvan naam ka ek cyclone India ke east coast ki taraf badh raha hai. 18 November ki raat iska forecast badal gaya. Toh yeh kahan aur kab takrayega, aur kise taiyaar rehna chahiye?
scenes.speak: Akvan नाम का एक cyclone India के east coast की तरफ बढ़ रहा है। 18 November की रात इसका forecast बदल गया। तो यह कहाँ और कब टकराएगा, और किसे तैयार रहना चाहिए?

scenes.say: 18 November ko raat saadhe nau baje, India Meteorological Department, yaani IMD, ne bataya ki Akvan Andhra Pradesh ke Narsapur se lagbhag 500 kilometre southeast mein tha. Yeh north-northwest ki taraf badh raha tha. Ab IMD ka kehna hai ki yeh Narsapur aur Odisha ke Puri ke beech, 20 November ko dopahar ke aas paas coast paar karega.
scenes.speak: 18 November को रात साढ़े नौ बजे, India Meteorological Department, यानी IMD, ने बताया कि Akvan Andhra Pradesh के Narsapur से लगभग 500 kilometre southeast में था। यह north-northwest की तरफ बढ़ रहा था। अब IMD का कहना है कि यह Narsapur और Odisha के Puri के बीच, 20 November को दोपहर के आस पास coast पार करेगा।

map.label: Expected landfall zone: Narsapur to Puri

scenes.say: Aur yeh pehle ke dar se kamzor rehne ki ummeed hai: severe cyclonic storm, very severe nahi. Hawa 90 se 100 kilometre per ghanta, jhonke 110 tak. North Andhra, Yanam aur south Odisha mein red alert hai.
scenes.speak: और यह पहले के डर से कमज़ोर रहने की उम्मीद है: severe cyclonic storm, very severe नहीं। हवा 90 से 100 kilometre per घंटा, झोंके 110 तक। North Andhra, Yanam और south Odisha में red alert है।

scenes.say: Odisha ne logon ko hatana shuru kar diya hai. Ganjam district ne ehtiyaat ke taur par 149 pregnant mahilaon ko health facilities aur maternity homes mein shift kiya hai.
scenes.speak: Odisha ने लोगों को हटाना शुरू कर दिया है। Ganjam district ने एहतियात के तौर पर 149 pregnant महिलाओं को health facilities और maternity homes में shift किया है।

scenes.say: Is response ko samajhne ke liye thoda peeche chaliye. India ke zyadatar cyclone Bay of Bengal mein bante hain, Arabian Sea ke har ek par lagbhag 4. Andhra Pradesh mein November 1977 aur May 1990 mein severe cyclone aaye the.

scenes.speak: अब इस storm से पहले की कहानी। Akvan इस season का तीसरा cyclone है, Arnab और Murasu के बाद। 17 November को उम्मीद थी कि यह 20 November को very severe storm बनके Andhra से टकराएगा। Odisha ने possible evacuation के लिए लगभग 2 लाख लोगों की list बनाई थी।

scenes.say: Toh naya forecast kyun matter karta hai? Pehla, crossing zone north ki taraf khisak gaya. 18 November ki subah tak reports Nellore se Visakhapatnam keh rahi thi. Ab yeh Narsapur se Puri hai, isliye north Andhra, Yanam aur south Odisha red alert par hain.
scenes.speak: तो नया forecast क्यों matter करता है? पहला, crossing zone north की तरफ खिसक गया। 18 November की सुबह तक reports Nellore से Visakhapatnam कह रही थीं। अब यह Narsapur से Puri है, इसलिए north Andhra, Yanam और south Odisha red alert पर हैं।

scenes.say: Doosra, kam hawa ka matlab hai hawa se kam nuksaan. Lekin baarish wind category par depend nahi karti. Coastal Andhra mein kuch jagahon par 19 aur 20 November ko extremely heavy rain ka forecast ab bhi hai. Srikakulam se Kakinada tak, 6 districts ko iske liye flag kiya gaya hai.
scenes.speak: दूसरा, कम हवा का मतलब है हवा से कम नुकसान। लेकिन बारिश wind category पर depend नहीं करती। Coastal Andhra में कुछ जगहों पर 19 और 20 November को extremely heavy rain का forecast अब भी है। Srikakulam से Kakinada तक, 6 districts को इसके लिए flag किया गया है।

scenes.speak: तीसरा, अंदर के इलाकों में भारी बारिश से flood और landslide आते हैं। इसलिए Odisha के Rayagada ने 55 landslide-prone और 148 flood-prone जगहों को map किया है।

scenes.say: Ab, kaun kaun shaamil hai? IMD forecast aur colour-coded alerts jaari karta hai. Odisha ke Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi evacuation lead kar rahe hain. East Coast Railway trains cancel aur reschedule kar raha hai. Aur Odisha ke State Selection Board ne 2 recruitment exams postpone kiye hain.
scenes.speak: अब, कौन कौन शामिल है? IMD forecast और colour-coded alerts जारी करता है। Odisha के Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi evacuation lead कर रहे हैं। East Coast Railway trains cancel और reschedule कर रहा है। और Odisha के State Selection Board ने 2 recruitment exams postpone किए हैं।

scenes.say: Numbers mein dekhiye. Pehle forecast tha 130 kilometre per ghante tak, jhonke 145 tak. Ab hai 100 tak, jhonke 110 tak.
scenes.speak: Numbers में देखिए। पहले forecast था 130 kilometre per घंटे तक, झोंके 145 तक। अब है 100 तक, झोंके 110 तक।

scenes.say: Odisha ke red-warning districts mein 47000 se zyada logon ko hataya gaya hai, inmein se zyadatar Ganjam mein. Yeh pehli list ke 2 lakh ke ek chauthai se thoda kam hai. Saaf nahi hai ki aur log hataye jayenge ya nahi. Lagbhag 3500 shelters taiyaar hain.
scenes.speak: Odisha के red-warning districts में 47000 से ज़्यादा लोगों को हटाया गया है, इनमें से ज़्यादातर Ganjam में। यह पहली list के 2 लाख के एक चौथाई से थोड़ा कम है। साफ़ नहीं है कि और लोग हटाए जाएँगे या नहीं। लगभग 3500 shelters तैयार हैं।

scenes.say: Ab woh ek baat jo yaad rakhni hai. Cyclone ki category uski wind speed se tay hoti hai. Baarish ek alag khatra hai. Kul baarish is par depend karti hai ki paani kitni tezi se girta hai, aur storm kitni der upar rukta hai.
scenes.speak: अब वो एक बात जो याद रखनी है। Cyclone की category उसकी wind speed से तय होती है। बारिश एक अलग खतरा है। कुल बारिश इस पर depend करती है कि पानी कितनी तेज़ी से गिरता है, और storm कितनी देर ऊपर रुकता है।

scenes.say: Step by step samjhiye. Pehla, category centre ke paas ki steady hawa hai. Doosra, hawa coast par sabse zor se lagti hai, phir andar jaate jaate kamzor padti hai. Teesra, baarish un cloud bands se girti hai jo centre se door tak phaile hote hain. Chautha, kul baarish yaani centimetre per ghanta, guna upar rehne ke ghante. Paanchva, yahi baarish nadiyon mein baadh laati hai aur pahadi dhalaan ko kamzor karti hai.
scenes.show: Wind at the coast; rain spreads inland
scenes.speak: Step by step समझिए। पहला, category centre के पास की steady हवा है। दूसरा, हवा coast पर सबसे ज़ोर से लगती है, फिर अंदर जाते जाते कमज़ोर पड़ती है। तीसरा, बारिश उन cloud bands से गिरती है जो centre से दूर तक फैले होते हैं। चौथा, कुल बारिश यानी centimetre per घंटा, गुना ऊपर रहने के घंटे। पाँचवाँ, यही बारिश नदियों में बाढ़ लाती है और पहाड़ी ढलान को कमज़ोर करती है।

scenes.say: Socho, do storm ek hi sheher ke upar hain. Storm A ki hawa tez hai, lekin woh jaldi nikal jaata hai. Maan lijiye 2 centimetre per ghanta, 6 ghante tak. Hua 12 centimetre. Storm B ki hawa kamzor hai, lekin woh dheere chalta hai. Maan lijiye dedh centimetre per ghanta, 15 ghante tak. Hua saadhe baais centimetre. Kamzor storm lagbhag dugni baarish girata hai.
scenes.show: Weaker storm, nearly twice the rain
scenes.speak: सोचो, दो storm एक ही शहर के ऊपर हैं। Storm A की हवा तेज़ है, लेकिन वो जल्दी निकल जाता है। मान लीजिए 2 centimetre per घंटा, 6 घंटे तक। हुआ 12 centimetre। Storm B की हवा कमज़ोर है, लेकिन वो धीरे चलता है। मान लीजिए डेढ़ centimetre per घंटा, 15 घंटे तक। हुआ साढ़े बाईस centimetre। कमज़ोर storm लगभग दुगनी बारिश गिराता है।

scenes.say: Toh ek aam galti hai: sochna ki downgrade hua cyclone ab khatarnak nahi hai. Downgrade hawa ke baare mein hai. Akvan ke red alerts ab bhi lage hain, aur coastal Andhra ke kuch hisson mein extremely heavy rain ka forecast ab bhi hai. Jaisa humare example ne dikhaya, kam hawa ka matlab kam baarish nahi.
scenes.speak: तो एक आम गलती है: सोचना कि downgrade हुआ cyclone अब खतरनाक नहीं है। Downgrade हवा के बारे में है। Akvan के red alerts अब भी लगे हैं, और coastal Andhra के कुछ हिस्सों में extremely heavy rain का forecast अब भी है। जैसा हमारे example ने दिखाया, कम हवा का मतलब कम बारिश नहीं।

scenes.say: Aapke liye iska kya matlab hai? Agar aap north coastal Andhra ya south Odisha mein hain, ya wahan ja rahe hain, toh 19 se 21 November ke hisaab se plan kijiye. Odisha ne 7 districts mein schools aur Anganwadi centres band kiye hain, aur 21 aur 23 November ke clerk exams postpone kar diye hain.
scenes.speak: आपके लिए इसका क्या मतलब है? अगर आप north coastal Andhra या south Odisha में हैं, या वहाँ जा रहे हैं, तो 19 से 21 November के हिसाब से plan कीजिए। Odisha ने 7 districts में schools और Anganwadi centres बंद किए हैं, और 21 और 23 November के clerk exams postpone कर दिए हैं।

scenes.say: Train se safar karne walon ke liye: Visakhapatnam se Kirandul wali trains 19 aur 20 November ko cancel hain. Landfall area ke paas trains ko landfall se lagbhag 3 ghante pehle aur baad tak regulate aur reschedule kiya jayega.

scenes.say: Aage kya dekhna hai? 19 aur 20 November ko coastal Andhra mein kuch jagahon par extremely heavy rain. 20 November ko dopahar ke aas paas Narsapur aur Puri ke beech landfall. Abhi pata nahi: Andhra kitne logon ko evacuate kar raha hai, flights par asar padega ya nahi, aur Odisha ka evacuation abhi bhi badh raha hai ya nahi. Aur haan, yeh forecast humein ek news report se mila hai, IMD ke apne text se nahi.
scenes.speak: आगे क्या देखना है? 19 और 20 November को coastal Andhra में कुछ जगहों पर extremely heavy rain। 20 November को दोपहर के आस पास Narsapur और Puri के बीच landfall। अभी पता नहीं: Andhra कितने लोगों को evacuate कर रहा है, flights पर असर पड़ेगा या नहीं, और Odisha का evacuation अभी भी बढ़ रहा है या नहीं। और हाँ, यह forecast हमें एक news report से मिला है, IMD के अपने text से नहीं।

stories.headline: Bangladesh faces Awami League arson and garment wage protests together
stories.question: Why is Bangladesh seeing both Awami League riots and a crackdown on garment workers?
stories.dek: These are two different fights. Activists of a banned party stormed a police station, and garment workers want their wage more than doubled. The new government is answering both with force.

so_far.text: Sheikh Hasina's Awami League ruled Bangladesh for 15 years until a student uprising forced her out on 5 August 2024. She fled to India. The interim government banned the party's activities in May 2025, and the party was barred from the 12 February 2026 election. The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) won that election in a landslide, and Tarique Rahman became prime minister. In early and mid November 2026, crude-bomb blasts and vehicle arson hit the country. The government blames the banned Awami League.

what_happened.text: On the evening of 17 November 2026, banned Awami League and Chhatra League activists stormed and burned Tungipara police station in Gopalganj. They acted after police arrested several party leaders and activists, and they freed the detainees. Police fired tear gas, sound grenades and rubber bullets, then withdrew. Activists burned vehicles, including two of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), and blocked the Gopalganj-Tungipara road. The home of BNP MP SM Zilany was set on fire the same night. Around the same time, garment workers demanding a higher minimum wage blocked highways, and police and 42 BGB platoons met them with tear gas, batons and drones.

steps.text: The Awami League's activities are banned until a tribunal finishes trying the party, and it was barred from the February 2026 election.
On 17 November police in Tungipara arrested several party leaders and activists; activists then stormed the station and freed the detainees.
The government calls the unrest planned sabotage; on 16 November Dhaka's police chief reportedly ordered police to fire on vehicle arsonists.
Separately, garment workers want the Tk 12,500 monthly minimum wage raised to Tk 30,000.
They blocked a highway on 12 November; more blockades followed the wage board's delay to 23 November, met by police and border troops.

history.text: The Awami League was founded on 23 June 1949. It led the Bengali language movement and the independence struggle, and formed Bangladesh's first government in 1971. So the party is tied to the birth of the country. In August 1975 its founding leader, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, was assassinated in a coup, and the party was folded into a body called BAKSAL. His daughter, Sheikh Hasina, became party president in 1981. She governed for 15 years, from 2009 to 2024. Those years saw democratic backsliding, and opposition parties boycotted or called unfair several elections, including the 2024 vote. In June 2024 students began a movement to reform job quotas. After Hasina's remarks on 14 July and attacks by the Chhatra League, the party's student wing, the protests turned deadly: 215 confirmed dead by 2 August, and unofficial tolls of 300 to 500. Hasina resigned on 5 August 2024 and fled to India. The interim government under Muhammad Yunus banned the Chhatra League in October 2024 and the Awami League's activities in May 2025. The ban lasts until the International Crimes Tribunal finishes its trial of the party. On 17 November 2025 that tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia, meaning without her present, for crimes against humanity over the 2024 crackdown. In February 2026 the BNP won an election the Awami League could not enter. So a party that ruled for 15 years is now banned from political activity until that tribunal finishes trying it.

lesson.concept: How a minimum wage floor is set and fought over
lesson.big_idea: A minimum wage is the lowest monthly pay the law allows. Raising it lifts every worker at the bottom at once, so the size of the rise decides who gains and who pays.

steps.title: The floor wage
steps.text: A minimum wage is the legal lowest pay for a job. As of 18 November 2026, Bangladesh's garment minimum is Tk 12,500 a month, about $100.

steps.title: A board reviews it
steps.text: The figure is not fixed forever. In Bangladesh a Minimum Wage Board meets to review it. Boards like this usually hear employers, workers and the government before suggesting a new figure.

steps.title: Each side does sums
steps.text: Workers compare the wage with what food and rent cost. Owners look at their wage bill: the number of workers multiplied by the wage each one earns.

steps.title: The gap is the fight
steps.text: Garment workers want Tk 30,000, which is 2.4 times the Tk 12,500 floor. The wider the gap between the demand and the floor, the harder the bargaining.

steps.title: Pressure while waiting
steps.text: Until the board decides, both sides push. Workers block roads; factories halt production or owners threaten closures. Each side is trying to shape the final number.

example.setup: Say a garment factory has 1,000 workers, all paid the minimum wage. The board must choose a figure somewhere between the Tk 12,500 floor and the workers' Tk 30,000 demand.

apply.text: That is the fight in Bangladesh in November 2026. Workers want Tk 30,000 instead of Tk 12,500. On 11 November production halted at 143 factories, and owners weighed closing 210. After the wage board meeting was delayed to 23 November, protesters blocked the N3, N4 and N5 highways and 37 factories shut. Police and 42 BGB platoons were sent in.

practice.q: Suppose the board settles at Tk 20,000. For a factory with 500 workers on the minimum, how much does the monthly wage bill rise?
practice.answer: Before: 500 × Tk 12,500 = Tk 62.5 lakh. New: 500 × Tk 20,000 = Tk 1 crore. Rise: Tk 1 crore − Tk 62.5 lakh = Tk 37.5 lakh a month. Each worker gains Tk 7,500, and the bill grows 1.6 times.

so_far.text: COP31, the UN's yearly climate summit, is meeting in Antalya, with Australia co-hosting alongside Turkey. It is scheduled to close on Friday 20 November 2026. On 16 November Australia released an 18-page first draft of the 'cover decision', the summit's main political statement. Chris Bowen, who leads the talks, said it 'won't be the final draft'. He promised at least one more draft before the week ends.

what_happened.text: The 16 November draft gives countries two choices on fossil fuels. One repeats the 2023 pledge of 'transitioning away'. The other calls for 'accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels'. Both could be dropped from the final deal. The draft also asks rich nations for at least $120 billion for adaptation, meaning help coping with climate damage. In a report published on 17 November, AP quoted a European official calling some provisions 'obviously unacceptable'. The official accused a bloc including Saudi Arabia and India of pushing obligations onto developed countries. The report carries no statement from India.

steps.text: A COP deal needs consensus of nearly 200 nations, so any country can hold out against wording it dislikes.
About 60 countries want clearer fossil-fuel commitments, but producing and developing economies resist, citing energy security, development and sovereignty.
So the draft offers two fossil-fuel options instead of one, and leaves the choice to the final days.
Side fights pile up too: adaptation money, the timing of IPCC reports and Turkey's electricity target each need agreement.
With the close set for 20 November, the hosts must find wording all accept, or let talks run over.

history.text:
The root is the Paris Agreement, adopted by consensus at COP21 on 12 December 2015. It aims to hold warming well below 2C and to try to limit it to 1.5C. Rich countries had also committed to mobilise $100 billion a year in climate finance by 2020. That pledge still underlies the fights over finance and adaptation money at COP31.

In September 2023 the first global stocktake, a formal check on progress, found the world off track. It said emissions must peak by 2025 to keep 1.5C within reach.

That set up COP28 in Dubai in December 2023. For the first time, a COP deal mentioned moving away from all fossil fuels. It asked countries to 'transition away' in a just, orderly and equitable way. It stopped short of a phase-out, which drew criticism. At the same summit, China and India did not sign a pledge to triple renewable energy capacity by 2030. That fits India's long-running resistance to uniform global targets.

Then the United States stepped back. Donald Trump signed a new Paris withdrawal order on 20 January 2025, and it took effect on 27 January 2026.

So COP31 inherited the question Dubai left open: go beyond 'transition away', or not.

lesson.concept: How consensus decides what a COP deal says
lesson.big_idea: A COP deal is not voted on. It passes only when no country formally objects, so the final text keeps only the words every country can live with.

steps.title: The host writes a draft
steps.text: The hosts draft a 'cover decision', the summit's main political statement. Australia released an 18-page first draft on 16 November and says at least one more draft follows before the week ends.

steps.title: Disagreements become options
steps.text: Where countries disagree, the draft lists choices side by side. On fossil fuels it offers two: repeat 2023's 'transitioning away', or 'accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels'.

steps.title: Consensus is not a vote
steps.text: Consensus means the text passes only if no country formally objects. It needs nearly 200 nations on board, so one determined country can block a line everyone else wants.

steps.title: Blocked lines get softened or cut
steps.text: When an option draws an objection, the hosts look for softer wording, or drop the line. That is why both fossil-fuel options could vanish from the final deal.

steps.title: Deadlines add pressure
steps.text: Talks have a scheduled end, here 20 November. Past COPs have often run days over while hosts hunt for wording that everyone can accept.

example.setup: Imagine a mini climate summit of 10 countries choosing the fossil-fuel line. Seven back a 'phase out', two prefer the older 'transition away', and one oil producer objects to anything new.
